dedupe_keys.name: fvessel inland waterway ais and video fusion benchmark

description: FVessel is a vessel detection, tracking and AIS-video fusion benchmark captured on the Wuhan segment of the Yangtze River. Yu Guo and collaborators publish data acquired using a shore camera and a Class-B AIS receiver under varied weather and bridge or riverside views. Version 1 documents 26 video sequences and 7,625 detection images; version 2 adds nine sequences. Files include MP4 video, AIS CSV tables, camera parameters, MOT-style text labels and image XML annotations. Ground-truth video is processed once per second, while AIS rows retain timestamps and the latest report within a ten-minute window. Exact full acquisition dates are not listed. The canonical Hugging Face page currently lists both version archives and is ungated, despite the older GitHub note requesting institutional email for version 2. Access is free; GitHub code uses MIT, but no separate archive licence was found in Hugging Face metadata. Anonymised vessel identifiers and incomplete AIS coverage limit linkage to real fleets. Simulation uses include validating inland-waterway perception and traffic observation models. No directly related catalogue record was identified.
